question:
A 24-year-old female patient is hospitalized for evaluation of worsening shortness of breath. She has
no significant past medical history. Her vital signs show a temperature of 37°C (98.6°F), heart rate of
115/min, respiratory rate of 21/min, and room air oxygen saturation of 99%. Heart examination reveals
accentuated S1 and S2 heart sounds, along with a grade 2/6 early systolic murmur that is most
prominent in the second right intercostal space. Cardiac catheterization reveals a mixed venous
oxygen saturation of 55% (normal range: 65-70%). What is the most probable underlying cause of her
breathlessness? Answer Choices: (A) Increased peripheral shunting (B) Increased pulmonary vascular
resistance (C) Right-to-left intracardiac shunt (D) Impaired oxygen diffusion capacity (E) Abnormal
hemoglobin with reduced oxygen affinity (F) Decreased hemoglobin concentration (G) Mitochondrial
dysfunction affecting oxygen utilization (H) Ventilation-perfusion mismatch (I) Decreased cardiac output
with preserved ejection fraction (J) Decreased left ventricular ejection fraction
 A. Abnormal hemoglobin with reduced oxygen affinity
B. Increased peripheral shunting
C. Decreased cardiac output with preserved ejection fraction
D. Impaired oxygen diffusion capacity
E. Decreased hemoglobin concentration
F. Mitochondrial dysfunction affecting oxygen utilization
G. Increased pulmonary vascular resistance
H. Right-to-left intracardiac shunt
I. Ventilation-perfusion mismatch
J. Decreased left ventricular ejection fraction
